title.value: Neural Fine-Tuning Search for Few-Shot Learning

TLDR.value: A stochastic neural architecture search algorithm that searches for the optimal configuration of layers in a pre-trained backbone architecture, to be adapted or fine-tuned.

abstract.value: In few-shot recognition, a classifier that has been trained on one set of classes is required to rapidly adapt and generalize to a disjoint, novel set of classes. To that end, recent studies have shown the efficacy of fine-tuning with carefully-crafted adaptation architectures. However this raises the question of: How can one design the optimal adaptation strategy? In this paper, we study this question through the lens of neural architecture search (NAS). Given a pre-trained neural network, our algorithm discovers the optimal arrangement of adapters, which layers to keep frozen, and which to fine-tune. We demonstrate the generality of our NAS method by applying it to both residual networks and vision transformers and report state-of-the-art performance on Meta-Dataset and Meta-Album.

primary_area.value: transfer learning, meta learning, and lifelong learning
